Gist: The stuck part was my own check, not the stepper. The stepper had already reloaded with your change: 象's marks are now underlined inside PARSE, and the list under OPERATORS is gone. My loop waiting on it never ended, so the turn hung until it was killed. The stepper is back on your latest turn.

**Why my check hung:** it waited for the newest turn to have 象's marks. That turn hadn't been read by 象 yet, so the condition could never come true, and I hadn't given the wait a time limit. Checking directly afterwards with a timeout showed the stepper had loaded all 89 frames.

**What your "operational words" turn looks like now:** in PARSE, the underlined phrases are "really supposed to", "operational words", "E.g.", "look for" (the quoted one), "CHIPWITS verb", "multiple tags" and "take the intersection". The OPERATORS block now lists only the operator words (the two "look for"s) and how each relates to 象's marks.

The change is committed as futon3c 2fed3224. The Python tests and all 9 Emacs tests pass, including a new one that checks an underline covers only its own phrase.
